description: Content rules checked by the backend (D27, D28). Construction status decides whether first-hand living experience is possible, so evidence, reviews and page wording must agree with it. Status is context for these checks; the page does not state it as a fact unless it comes from a verified primary record. Source reviews show the author's own words.

wording.note: Deterministic backstop for the client's own page text (overview, advantages, considerations, questions); A09 QA checks meaning as well. Terms match as whole words, case-insensitive. Before possession they block approval; in a partially ready project they ask the editor to name the phase. Source reviews are the authors' words and are checked through their perspective instead.

preferred_terms.partially_ready: residents of the ready phase (name it) and buyers awaiting other phases

review_text.note: Displayed review text contains no dashes or hyphens (product owner, 28 Sep 2026). A11 removes them with the punctuation_normalised rendering, which may change punctuation only; every word stays the author's.

status_checks.note: D63: further checks of a claim or review against the status in force on its date. Each applies only when occupancy was possible then (ready, or the claim's ready phase).
